The game features the 'Mensch' (Queen of Clubs) as a permanent highest trump, similar to other games in the Ombre/Solo family. Players bid for the right to choose trumps and must make their contract.
MÃ«nsch is a Swiss Jass game, part of the larger Jass family that originated in the Netherlands and spread to Switzerland. It shares ancestry with games like Ombre and Solo.
4 players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.

36-card Jass deck (6 through Ace in four suits: Acorns, Shields, Flowers, Bells). Can use standard deck with 5s and below removed. Ranking in trumps: Under (Jack), 9, Ace, King, Ober (Queen), Banner (10), 8, 7, 6. In non-trump: Ace, King, Ober, Under, Banner, 9, 8, 7, 6.
36-card Jass deck or modified standard deck, score sheet.
9 cards to each player, dealt in packets of 3.

items.text: Mënsch Luxembourg: Luxembourg variant with different bidding conventions.
Schafkopf-Mensch: Bavarian-influenced variant with different card ranks.
